summary: Taxonomy is a full-stack Next.js 13 App Router demo: a marketing site, blog and docs built from MDX with Contentlayer, plus an authenticated dashboard where users write posts in Editor.js. NextAuth (GitHub + Postmark magic links, JWT sessions) handles auth, Prisma on MySQL stores users and posts, and Stripe Checkout, the billing portal and webhooks gate a Pro plan that lifts the 3-post limit.

nodes.label: Marketing, Blog & Docs
nodes.summary: The root layout (fonts, theme, metadata) and the public route groups: (marketing) landing, pricing and blog pages, and (docs) documentation and guides rendered from Contentlayer MDX.

nodes.label: Dashboard & Editor
nodes.summary: Authenticated server components under (dashboard) and (editor): the post list, billing and settings pages, and the Editor.js editor page, which loads a post only if the current user is its author.

nodes.label: UI Components
nodes.summary: Shared React components used by every route group: Radix-based primitives in components/ui, navigation, the post editor and item rows, the billing form, the user auth form and MDX renderers.

nodes.label: Login & Register Pages
nodes.summary: The (auth) route group with the login and register screens. They host the user auth form that starts the GitHub OAuth or email magic-link flow.

nodes.label: Auth (NextAuth + Middleware)
nodes.summary: authOptions configures NextAuth with the Prisma adapter, a GitHub provider, a Postmark-backed email provider and JWT sessions whose callback reloads the user from the DB. middleware.ts redirects unauthenticated visitors away from /dashboard and /editor.

nodes.label: Posts API
nodes.summary: Route handlers for listing and creating posts (enforcing the free-plan limit of 3) and for updating or deleting a single post after an ownership check. Bodies are validated with zod schemas from lib/validations.

nodes.label: User & Billing API
nodes.summary: PATCH /api/users/[userId] updates the display name, and GET /api/users/stripe returns either a Stripe billing-portal URL (Pro users) or a Checkout URL that carries the userId in metadata.

nodes.label: Stripe Webhook
nodes.summary: Verifies the Stripe signature, then on checkout.session.completed links the subscription to the user, and on invoice.payment_succeeded extends stripeCurrentPeriodEnd.

nodes.label: OG Image API
nodes.summary: Edge route that renders Open Graph images with @vercel/og from validated heading/type/mode query parameters, using bundled fonts.

nodes.label: Subscriptions & Stripe Client
nodes.summary: getUserSubscriptionPlan derives isPro from the stored Stripe price and period end (with a 1-day grace period) and merges in the free/pro plan definitions. lib/stripe.ts holds the configured Stripe SDK client.

nodes.label: Prisma / MySQL
nodes.summary: schema.prisma defines NextAuth's Account/Session/User/VerificationToken models, Stripe billing columns on User, and Post with Editor.js JSON content. lib/db.ts exports a PrismaClient singleton that is cached on globalThis in development to survive hot reloads.

nodes.label: Shared Utilities & Validation
nodes.summary: cn() class merging, date formatting, absoluteUrl from NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, the MDX table-of-contents builder, custom errors and the zod schemas for auth, posts and users.

nodes.label: Config & Environment
nodes.summary: Typed env validation (env.mjs), site/docs/dashboard/marketing navigation config, Next.js with Contentlayer, Tailwind, and package.json scripts.

bugs.title: Unauthenticated requests pass the post ownership check
bugs.description: verifyCurrentUserHasAccessToPost (lines 83-92) counts posts `where: { id: postId, authorId: session?.user.id }`. With no session, authorId is `undefined`, and Prisma treats an undefined filter as absent, so the query becomes `where: { id: postId }` and returns 1 for any existing post. middleware.ts only matches /dashboard, /editor, /login and /register, so a request to /api/posts/[postId] with no cookie can DELETE or PATCH any post whose id it knows.
bugs.suggestedFix: Return false early when there is no session: `if (!session?.user?.id) return false`, then query with the real id. Respond 401 instead of 403 for missing auth. Add a route test that calls DELETE without a session and expects 401.

bugs.title: JWT callback resolves identity by a possibly-empty email
bugs.description: On every token refresh the jwt callback runs `db.user.findFirst({ where: { email: token.email } })` and replaces the token with that user's id. The email column is nullable (schema.prisma line 48), and GitHub accounts without a public verified email produce a null email. `email: null` matches any other user with a null email, and an undefined email drops the filter so findFirst returns the first user. In both cases the session can end up with another account's id. It also costs a DB round-trip on every session read.
bugs.suggestedFix: Look up by the stable id instead: on sign-in `user` is set, so copy `token.id = user.id`; on later calls query `findUnique({ where: { id: token.id } })`, and never query when the key is missing.

bugs.title: invoice.payment_succeeded can arrive before the subscription is linked
bugs.description: Stripe doesn't guarantee event order. The first invoice.payment_succeeded often arrives before checkout.session.completed has stored stripeSubscriptionId, so `db.user.update({ where: { stripeSubscriptionId } })` finds no row and Prisma throws. Nothing catches it, so the handler returns 500 and Stripe retries with backoff. The checkout branch (line 37) also passes `session?.metadata?.userId` without checking it, which throws the same way when metadata is missing.
bugs.suggestedFix: Wrap each branch in try/catch. For invoices, use updateMany (no throw on 0 rows), or resolve the user by stripeCustomerId and fall back to the subscription's metadata. Return 200 for events you deliberately ignore and log unexpected misses.

bugs.title: Every webhook payload is cast to Checkout.Session
bugs.description: `event.data.object as Stripe.Checkout.Session` runs before the event type is checked, so the invoice.payment_succeeded branch treats a Stripe.Invoice as a checkout session. Reading `.subscription` happens to work because both types have that field, but the cast hides type errors and will silently break when Stripe changes the invoice shape (newer API versions move it).
bugs.suggestedFix: Narrow per branch: `if (event.type === 'invoice.payment_succeeded') { const invoice = event.data.object as Stripe.Invoice; ... }`, or switch on event.type so TypeScript's discriminated union picks the right type.

bugs.title: Free-plan post limit can be exceeded with concurrent requests
bugs.description: POST counts the user's posts (line 55) and creates a new one (line 69) as separate queries. Several parallel requests from a free user can all see count < 3 and each create a post, bypassing the 3-post limit.
bugs.suggestedFix: Run the count and the create in one `db.$transaction` with Serializable isolation (or SELECT … FOR UPDATE on the user row), or enforce the limit with a DB-side check.

bugs.title: Billing logic is excluded from type-checking
bugs.description: The file starts with `// @ts-nocheck`. As a result `isPro` is typed as boolean but evaluates to `string | null | boolean` (the `&&` returns stripePriceId's value), and `getTime() + 86_400_000` on a possibly-undefined date isn't flagged. This is the function every paywall decision depends on.
bugs.suggestedFix: Remove @ts-nocheck and write `const isPro = Boolean(user.stripePriceId && user.stripeCurrentPeriodEnd && user.stripeCurrentPeriodEnd.getTime() + 86_400_000 > Date.now())`. Add unit tests for expired, active and grace-period cases.

walkthrough.title: Start here: stack and environment
walkthrough.explanation: Skim the README and package.json, then open env.mjs. It's the typed entry point for every secret the code reads through `env.` (GitHub OAuth, Postmark templates, Stripe keys and webhook secret, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL). prisma/schema.prisma additionally reads DATABASE_URL.

walkthrough.title: Entry point: the root layout and route groups
walkthrough.explanation: app/layout.tsx wraps everything (fonts, theme, toaster, analytics). The folders in parentheses under app/ are route groups: (marketing), (docs), (auth), (dashboard) and (editor) each get their own layout without changing URLs.

walkthrough.title: Auth: NextAuth options and the middleware gate
walkthrough.explanation: lib/auth.ts is the single source of auth config (providers, JWT callbacks), and server code calls getServerSession(authOptions). middleware.ts protects page routes only; API routes must check the session themselves.

walkthrough.title: Core logic: the Posts API and plan limits
walkthrough.explanation: The POST handler shows the app's main pattern: get the session, load the subscription plan, enforce the free-tier limit, validate with zod, then write through Prisma. [postId]/route.ts adds ownership checks for edits and deletes.

walkthrough.title: Data layer: Prisma schema and client
walkthrough.explanation: User carries both NextAuth relations and Stripe billing columns, and Post stores Editor.js output as JSON. lib/db.ts reuses one PrismaClient across hot reloads in dev.

walkthrough.title: Billing: checkout, webhook, plan derivation
walkthrough.explanation: Follow the money: /api/users/stripe creates a Checkout session with the userId in metadata, the webhook writes subscription ids and period end, and lib/subscription.ts turns those columns into isPro.

walkthrough.title: Good first contribution: close the post-access hole
walkthrough.explanation: Make verifyCurrentUserHasAccessToPost return false when there's no session (Prisma ignores undefined filters), switch the missing-auth response to 401, and add a test. It's a two-line fix to a high-severity issue with an obvious regression test.
